faqs.q: Which Articles deal with the parliamentary system of government at the Centre?
Which Articles deal with the parliamentary system of government in the states?
In a parliamentary system, the executive is responsible to which organ of government?
Which of the following is NOT another name for the parliamentary system of government?
faqs.e: Fixed executive system is another name for the presidential system, not the parliamentary system.

faqs.q:
Consider the following countries:
(I) Britain
(II) USA
(III) Japan
Which of the above follow a parliamentary system of government?
faqs.e: USA follows the presidential system, not the parliamentary system.

faqs.q: Which of the following countries follows a presidential system of government?
Who described the parliamentary system as the 'cabinet system'?
faqs.e: Jennings used this term because the cabinet is the nucleus of power in a parliamentary system.

faqs.q: The term 'Westminster model of government' is derived from which of the following?

options.a: The location of the British Parliament
options.c: The name of the first British Prime Minister

faqs.a: The location of the British Parliament

faqs.q: The Prime Minister was traditionally described as 'primus inter pares' in relation to which body?
faqs.e: 'Primus inter pares' means 'first among equals.'

faqs.q: Which term has later political analysts like Crossman and Mackintosh used to describe the British system of government?
In the parliamentary system, who is the nominal executive?
Which Article provides for a council of ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President?

Consider the following statements:
(I) The advice tendered by the council of ministers is binding on the President
(II) The President is the de facto executive
(III) The Prime Minister is the de jure executive
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The President is the de jure (nominal) executive, and the Prime Minister is the de facto (real) executive, so statements II and III are reversed.

faqs.q: Under majority party rule, who appoints other ministers besides the Prime Minister?

options.c: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.d: The President, on the advice of the Prime Minister

faqs.a: The President, on the advice of the Prime Minister

faqs.q: Collective responsibility of ministers is provided for under which Article?
Through which mechanism can the Lok Sabha remove the council of ministers from office?
A minister who is not a member of Parliament ceases to be a minister after which period?
Which of the following leadership roles is NOT held by the Prime Minister?

options.c: Leader of the council of ministers
options.d: Leader of the party in power

faqs.q: On whose recommendation can the President dissolve the Lok Sabha before the expiry of its term?
Who administers the oath of secrecy to ministers before they enter office?

options.b: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

faqs.q: In the American presidential system, the President governs with the help of an advisory body popularly known as what?
For how many years is the American President elected?
The American President can be removed from office only through which process?

options.a: Impeachment for a grave unconstitutional act
options.c: A resolution of the Senate alone

faqs.a: Impeachment for a grave unconstitutional act

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the American presidential system:
(I) The President and secretaries are not responsible to the Congress for their acts
(II) The President can dissolve the House of Representatives
(III) The doctrine of separation of powers is the basis of the presidential system
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The American President cannot dissolve the House of Representatives, the lower house of the Congress.

faqs.q: Members of the American Kitchen Cabinet are best described as which of the following?
Which merit of the parliamentary system did Dr. Jennings describe with the phrase "the leader of the opposition is the alternative prime minister"?
Under the parliamentary system, executive authority is vested in a group of individuals rather than a single person. This is cited as a safeguard against which of the following?
Which of the following devices is used by Parliament to exercise control over ministers under the parliamentary system?
Which of the following governments is cited as an example of instability under the parliamentary system?
The Janata Government headed by Morarji Desai in 1977 is cited as an example illustrating which demerit of the parliamentary system?
Who complained of the "dictatorship of the cabinet" as a demerit of the parliamentary system?
Which scholar remarked that the parliamentary system gives the executive "an opportunity for tyranny"?
Bagehot described the cabinet using which of the following phrases?

options.b: "A hyphen that joins the buckle that binds the executive and legislative departments together"

faqs.a: "A hyphen that joins the buckle that binds the executive and legislative departments together"
faqs.e: This remark illustrates the demerit that the parliamentary system goes against the theory of separation of powers.

faqs.q: Under the parliamentary system, the Prime Minister's choice of ministers is restricted to which of the following?
faqs.e: This restriction is cited as the basis for the demerit termed "government by amateurs," since external talent cannot be inducted as ministers.

faqs.q: Which committee examined whether India's parliamentary system should be replaced by a presidential system?
faqs.e: The committee was appointed in 1975 and concluded that there was no need to replace the parliamentary system.

faqs.q: Which member of the Constituent Assembly favoured the adoption of the presidential system for India?
Which leader argued in the Constituent Assembly that India's constitutional traditions had "become Parliamentary" and there was no need to "buy a novel experience"?
According to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, a democratic executive must satisfy which two conditions?
As per Dr. Ambedkar's observation in the Constituent Assembly, the Draft Constitution's parliamentary system preferred which of the following?

Consider the following reasons cited for India adopting the parliamentary system:
(I) Familiarity with the system due to its operation during British rule
(II) Need to avoid legislative-executive conflicts
(III) Nature of Indian society as a heterogeneous and plural state
Which of the above is/are correct?
India differs from the British parliamentary model in having which of the following?

options.b: A republican system with an elected Head of State

faqs.a: A republican system with an elected Head of State

faqs.q: Unlike in Britain, the Indian Parliament is not supreme because of which of the following?

options.b: The presence of a written Constitution
options.d: The absence of a Prime Minister

faqs.a: The presence of a written Constitution
faqs.e: A written Constitution, federal system, judicial review, and fundamental rights together restrict Parliament's supremacy in India, unlike Britain's doctrine of parliamentary sovereignty.

faqs.q: In Britain, the Prime Minister must be a member of which House of Parliament?

Consider the following statements:
(I) In India, a person who is not a member of Parliament can be appointed as a minister for a maximum of six months
(II) In Britain, ministers are required to countersign the official acts of the Head of State
(III) India has a system of legal responsibility of the minister similar to Britain
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: India has no system of legal responsibility of the minister, and ministers in India are not required to countersign the Head of State's official acts, unlike in Britain.

faqs.q: Which institution of the British cabinet system, formed by the opposition party to prepare for future ministerial office, does not exist in India?
Which Amendment Acts made the ministerial advice binding on the President?
faqs.e: The 42nd Amendment Act was enacted in 1976 and the 44th Amendment Act in 1978.

faqs.q: Who propounded the theory of separation of powers, referenced in the context of the parliamentary system's demerits?
In which book did Montesquieu propound the theory of separation of powers?
faqs.e: The Spirit of Laws was published in 1748.

faqs.q:
Consider the following Prime Ministers who were members of the Rajya Sabha at the time:
(I) Indira Gandhi (1966)
(II) Deve Gowda (1996)
(III) Manmohan Singh (2004)
Which of the above is/are correctly identified as having been members of the Rajya Sabha?
faqs.e: This illustrates that, unlike Britain, the Indian Prime Minister may belong to either House of Parliament.

faqs.q: Which feature of the parliamentary system is compared to the presidential system as "fusion of powers" versus "separation of powers"?

options.b: The executive being part of the legislature

faqs.a: The executive being part of the legislature
faqs.e: This is presented as the key structural distinction underlying the parliamentary and presidential systems' comparative features.

rows: President and legislators elected separately for a fixed term
Dissolution of the Lower House possible
No dissolution of the Lower House
Merits: Harmony between legislature and executive, responsible government, prevents despotism, wide representation
Demerits: Conflict between legislature and executive, non-responsible government, may lead to autocracy, narrow representation
Demerits: Unstable government, no continuity of policies, against separation of powers, government by amateurs
Merits: Stable government, definiteness in policies, based on separation of powers, government by experts

faqs.q: Governments are classified into unitary and federal on the basis of the nature of relations between which two entities?

options.a: The Centre and the Election Commission
options.d: The national government and the regional governments

faqs.a: The national government and the regional governments

faqs.q: In a unitary government, the regional governments derive their authority from which of the following?
Which of the following countries has a unitary model of government?
Which of the following countries has a federal model of government?
In a federal model, the regional government is also known by which of the following names?
The term 'federation' is derived from which Latin word?
faqs.e: Foedus means 'treaty or agreement'.

faqs.q: In Switzerland, the units of the federation are known by which of the following names?
In Russia, the units of the federation are known by which of the following names?
A federation formed when militarily weak or economically backward independent states come together to form a strong union is formed by which method?
A federation formed when a big unitary state grants autonomy to its provinces is formed by which method?
Which country is considered the first and oldest federation in the world?
In which year was the US federation formed?
faqs.e: The US federation was formed following the American Revolution, and originally comprised 13 states.

faqs.q: In which year was the Canadian Federation formed?
faqs.e: The Canadian Federation originally comprised 4 provinces at its formation.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements:
(I) A federal government has a written Constitution
(II) A unitary government's Constitution may be written or unwritten
(III) A federal government has an unwritten Constitution
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: A federal government requires a written Constitution; it is a unitary government whose Constitution may be written (France) or unwritten (Britain).

faqs.q: Which of the following is a feature of a federal government but not necessarily of a unitary government?
In a unitary government, the legislature may be bicameral or unicameral. Which country is cited as an example of a unicameral legislature under a unitary government?
Which two main reasons led the framers of the Indian Constitution to adopt a federal system?

options.c: Large size of the country and its socio-cultural diversity

faqs.a: Large size of the country and its socio-cultural diversity

faqs.q: The term 'federation' appears in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
faqs.e: Instead, Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States'.

faqs.q: As per Article 1, India is described as which of the following?

According to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the phrase 'Union of States' was preferred over 'Federation of States' to indicate which of the following?
(I) The Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among the states
(II) The states have no right to secede from the federation
(III) The states have equal representation in the Rajya Sabha
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Equal representation of states in the Rajya Sabha is not among Ambedkar's stated reasons.

faqs.q: The Indian federal system is based on which model?
The Canadian model differs fundamentally from the American model in which respect?

options.d: It establishes a very strong centre

faqs.a: It establishes a very strong centre

faqs.q:
Consider the following respects in which the Indian federation resembles the Canadian federation:
(I) Formation by way of disintegration
(II) Preference for the term 'Union'
(III) Centralising tendency
Which of the above is/are correct?

rows: Single government, which may create regional governments

Division of powers between national and regional government
No division of powers; all powers vested in the national government

Constitution may be rigid (France) or flexible (Britain)
Judiciary may or may not be independent
Legislature may be bicameral (Britain) or unicameral (China)

faqs.q: The Constitution establishes a dual polity consisting of which two levels of government?
The Union government primarily deals with matters such as defence, foreign affairs, currency, and communication. These are matters of which kind of importance?
State governments primarily look after matters such as public order, agriculture, health, and local government. These are matters of which kind of importance?
The Indian Constitution is often described as which of the following, in terms of its length?

options.c: The shortest Constitution in the world
options.d: The lengthiest Constitution in the world

faqs.a: The lengthiest Constitution in the world

faqs.q: How many Articles did the Indian Constitution originally contain?
faqs.e: The Constitution's size has grown considerably since 1950 through amendments.

faqs.q: At present, the Indian Constitution consists of approximately how many Articles?
faqs.e: The Constitution presently has 506 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.

faqs.q: The powers between the Centre and the states are divided in terms of which Lists, contained in the Seventh Schedule?

options.b: Central List, Regional List and Joint List
options.c: Union List, State List and Concurrent List
options.d: Union List, State List and Residuary List

faqs.a: Union List, State List and Concurrent List

faqs.q: How many subjects does the Union List presently consist of?
How many subjects does the State List presently consist of?
How many subjects does the Concurrent List presently consist of?
In case of a conflict between a Central law and a state law on a subject in the Concurrent List, which law prevails?

options.d: The matter goes to the President

faqs.q: Subjects not mentioned in the Union, State, or Concurrent Lists are known as which of the following, and are given to whom?

options.b: Reserved subjects, given to the Rajya Sabha
options.c: Residuary subjects, given to the states
options.d: Residuary subjects, given to the Centre

faqs.a: Residuary subjects, given to the Centre

faqs.q: If a law made by the Centre or a state does not conform to the Constitution, which authority can declare it invalid?

options.a: The Supreme Court or the High Courts through judicial review

faqs.a: The Supreme Court or the High Courts through judicial review

faqs.q: Provisions concerned with the federal structure, such as Centre-state relations and judicial organisation, can be amended only through which process?

options.a: An executive order of the President
options.b: Special majority of Parliament and approval of half the state legislatures
options.d: A unanimous resolution of all state legislatures

faqs.a: Special majority of Parliament and approval of half the state legislatures

faqs.q: The rigidity of the Constitution with respect to federal provisions is primarily meant to protect which two features?

options.b: Division of powers and supremacy of the Constitution

faqs.a: Division of powers and supremacy of the Constitution

faqs.q: The Constitution establishes an independent judiciary headed by which body?

Consider the following purposes of an independent judiciary under the Constitution:
(I) To protect the supremacy of the Constitution through judicial review
(II) To settle disputes between the Centre and the states or between states
(III) To conduct elections to the Central and state legislatures
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Conducting elections is a function of the Election Commission, not the judiciary.

faqs.q: Which of the following measures is cited as making the judiciary independent of the government?
The Constitution provides for a bicameral legislature consisting of which two Houses?
Which House of Parliament represents the states of the Indian Federation?
The Rajya Sabha, despite being a less powerful chamber, is required to maintain the federal equilibrium by performing which function?

options.c: Protecting the interests of the states against undue interference of the Centre

faqs.a: Protecting the interests of the states against undue interference of the Centre

faqs.q: The division of powers in India is considered highly inequitable from the federal angle mainly because of which of the following?

options.a: States have overriding authority over the Concurrent List
options.b: The Union List contains more subjects than the State List
options.c: The State List contains more subjects than the Union List
options.d: The Concurrent List is larger than both other lists

faqs.a: The Union List contains more subjects than the State List

faqs.q: Residuary powers in India are vested with which of the following, unlike in the US?
The Parliament can change the area, boundaries, or name of any state through which kind of majority?
The Indian Federation has been described as which of the following?

options.a: An indestructible Union of destructible states
options.b: A destructible Union of destructible states
options.c: An indestructible Union of indestructible states
options.d: A destructible Union of indestructible states

faqs.a: An indestructible Union of destructible states

faqs.q: The American Federation, in contrast to the Indian Federation, has been described as which of the following?

options.a: A destructible Union of destructible states
options.b: A destructible Union of indestructible states
options.c: An indestructible Union of destructible states
options.d: An indestructible Union of indestructible states

faqs.a: An indestructible Union of indestructible states

faqs.q: In India, unlike in a typical federation, states do not have the right to which of the following?
Which erstwhile Indian state was the only exception to having its own separate state Constitution?
faqs.e: This special status existed by virtue of Article 370, until 2019.

faqs.q: In the US, unlike in India, which of the following bodies can also propose a constitutional amendment?
Representation of states in the Rajya Sabha is based on which of the following?
Membership of states in the Rajya Sabha varies within which range?
How many members does the American Senate have in total?
How many senators does each American state send to the Senate, reflecting the principle of equality of representation?
During an emergency under the Indian Constitution, the federal structure temporarily converts into which kind of structure?
How many types of emergencies does the Indian Constitution stipulate?

Which of the following federal countries has dual citizenship, unlike India?
The Indian Constitution establishes an integrated judicial system with which court at the top?
In the US, unlike in India, laws are enforced through which kind of court system?

options.a: A double system of federal and state judiciary

faqs.a: A double system of federal and state judiciary

faqs.q: Which of the following are examples of All-India Services common to both the Centre and the states?
Members of the All-India Services are recruited and trained by which authority?

options.a: The Union Public Service Commission independently of the Centre

faqs.q: Which constitutional authority audits the accounts of both the Central government and the states?

options.c: The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India

faqs.q: Unlike the American Constitution, which provided for an elected head in the states, India adopted the appointed-governor system from which country?

Over reserved state bills, the President enjoys which kind of veto?
Which constitutional expert described the Indian Constitution as "quasi-federal"?
K.C. Wheare described the Indian Union as which of the following?

options.a: A unitary state with subsidiary federal features
options.b: A federal state with subsidiary unitary features

faqs.q:
According to K. Santhanam, which two factors have increased the unitary bias of the Constitution?
(I) Dominance of the Centre in the financial sphere and dependence of states on Central grants
(II) The emergence of a powerful erstwhile planning commission
(III) The absence of an independent judiciary
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Santhanam did not cite the absence of an independent judiciary as a factor; the judiciary is in fact a recognised federal feature of the Constitution.

faqs.q: In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by which body?
Which political scientist characterised the Indian system as "extremely federal"?
Which political scientist termed the Indian federal system a "bargaining federalism"?
Ivor Jennings described the Indian Constitution as which of the following?

options.d: A federation with a strong centralising tendency

faqs.a: A federation with a strong centralising tendency

faqs.q: Which scholar described India as a case "sui generis," meaning unique in character?
Granville Austin, an American constitutional expert, described Indian federalism using which term?
In which case did the Supreme Court characterise federalism as a 'basic feature' of the Constitution?
faqs.e: The case was decided in 1994. In this judgement, states were described as entities with an independent constitutional existence in relation to the Centre.

faqs.q: Federalism in India represents a compromise between which two conflicting considerations?

options.c: Normal division of powers and the need for national integrity under exceptional circumstances

faqs.a: Normal division of powers and the need for national integrity under exceptional circumstances
